mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where the possession gap between the two sides (Team B FOR minus Team A FOR) exceeds a threshold derived from the long-run averages. Within those matches, measure whether Team B's shots FOR and shots_on_target FOR co-move upward while Team A's shots FOR remains suppressed.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: As the cross-team possession gap widens in favour of Team B, Team B's shots and shots_on_target rise above their long-run means while Team A's shots remain at or below their long-run mean — a joint asymmetric co-movement across both observables and both teams simultaneously.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: When Team B holds a large possession advantage over Team A (as seen in recent matches where Team B averaged ~63% possession vs Team A's ~41%), Team B's shot volume rises sharply relative to its long-run average, while Team A's shots-against also rises sharply. The joint relationship between the possession imbalance across both teams and the resulting shot differential is not captured by either team's possession or shots in isolation.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (possession and shots) measured for two different teams simultaneously, and testing an asymmetric cross-team relationship. It cannot be reduced to one team's possession vs one band, nor to one team's shots vs one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: In matches where Team A's fouls FOR (committed) is above a threshold, measure whether Team B's ratio of shots_on_target to shots is lower than in matches where Team A's fouls are below that threshold, controlling for Team B's raw shot volume.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's shots_on_target-to-shots ratio is suppressed in matches where Team A's foul rate is elevated, even when Team B's total shot count remains high — a non-linear joint relationship across two distinct observables from two different teams.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shot-to-shots-on-target conversion ratio (shot quality / accuracy) co-varies with Team A's defensive foul rate. When Team A commits more fouls (disrupting Team B's build-up), Team B's shots_on_target as a share of total shots may be suppressed even when raw shot volume is high. This joint relationship between Team A's fouls-committed and Team B's shots vs shots_on_target ratio is structurally richer than either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a joint relationship between one team's fouls (Team A FOR) and the other team's shots vs shots_on_target ratio (Team B), which is an asymmetric cross-team, two-observable interaction not reducible to any single-observable mirror or single-band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Split matches into first-half and second-half corner counts for both teams. Condition on Team A's historical tendency to concede more corners in the second half (AGAINST SECOND_HALF vs FIRST_HALF). Within those matches, test whether Team B's second-half corner count rises disproportionately relative to its first-half count compared to matches against teams that do not show this pattern.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's second-half corner count rises above its first-half count more sharply when facing opponents (like Team A) who structurally concede more corners in the second half — a within-match half-level interaction between two teams' corner tendencies across halves.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B generates substantially more corners in the second half than the first half (long-run 2H mean ~3.08 vs 1H mean ~2.52), while Team A generates fewer corners overall and concedes more corners recently. The joint within-match half-level split of corner production for Team B, conditioned on Team A's corner-conceding tendency, tests whether Team B's second-half corner surge is amplified when facing a team that structurally concedes more corners in the second half.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a within-match half-level split (first half vs second half) jointly conditioned on both teams' half-specific corner tendencies. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band; it requires two half-period observations and a cross-team conditioning dimension simultaneously.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Identify historical match contexts where the attacking team's recent-5 shots, shots_on_target, and possession all simultaneously exceed their long-run means, while the defending team's recent-5 shots-against, shots_on_target-against all simultaneously exceed their long-run means. Measure whether goals FOR the attacking team in such jointly-aligned contexts are elevated relative to contexts where only one or two of these observables are co-aligned.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Goals scored by the attacking team rise as the number of simultaneously co-aligned attacking/defensive observable pairs increases — a threshold or saturation effect where joint multi-observable alignment produces a stronger signal than any single observable's recent deviation alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's recent form shows a simultaneous deterioration across multiple defensive observables (shots against rising from ~14.9 to ~21.0, shots_on_target against rising from ~5.4 to ~6.6, goals against rising from ~1.79 to ~2.0, possession dropping from ~47% to ~40.8%) while Team B's recent form shows simultaneous improvement across multiple attacking observables (shots rising from ~14.5 to ~23.6, shots_on_target rising from ~5.7 to ~7.2, possession rising from ~53% to ~63.4%). The joint co-movement of multiple observables in the same direction for both teams simultaneously — one deteriorating defensively, one improving offensively — is a multi-observable regime signal not captured by any single observable's recent vs long-run comparison.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This mechanism requires joint conditioning on three or more distinct observables (shots, shots_on_target, possession) for both teams simultaneously, testing a threshold/saturation structure. It is not reducible to any single observable's recent vs long-run comparison or any single-band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: In historical matches where the home team's goals-against second-half rate exceeds its first-half rate AND the away team's goals-for second-half rate exceeds its first-half rate, measure whether the total second-half goal count (and cards_2h as a proxy for match intensity/state) is elevated relative to matches where only one or neither of these half-asymmetries holds.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half goals and cards_2h are jointly elevated when both teams simultaneously exhibit a second-half concentration in goals-against (home) and goals-for (away) — a compounding within-match half-state interaction that saturates beyond what either team's half-split alone would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's second-half goals-against rate (long-run ~1.056 per match) substantially exceeds its first-half goals-against rate (~0.732), while Team B's second-half goals-for rate (~1.239) substantially exceeds its first-half goals-for rate (~0.662). The joint within-match half-level asymmetry — where one team's defensive vulnerability is concentrated in the second half and the other team's attacking output is also concentrated in the second half — creates a compounding within-match state interaction. This is distinct from either team's half-split in isolation and requires conditioning on both simultaneously.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two teams' half-level splits for two different observables (goals and cards_2h), testing a compounding within-match state interaction. It is not reducible to a single observable's half split or a single-band conditioning.
